extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (agents/attorneys) seeking to accelerate examination using the USPTO PPH program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for requesting fast-track examination via the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) at the USPTO (and corresponding offices), including eligibility requirements, required documents, strategic considerations, comparisons to other acceleration options, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: First substantive Office action received in about 2-5 months (vs. typical 18-24 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key benefit of PPH is faster first substantive action; USPTO statistics list average first action pendency for PPH as ~7.5 months compared with 18-24 months for standard applications. Use PPH when obtaining an earlier, quicker substantive action is a priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: No added USPTO fee for filing PPH request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH itself has no additional USPTO fee, making it cost-attractive compared with other acceleration programs (e.g., Track One costs $4,200). Consider filing fees and practitioner costs when comparing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Success Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: ~10% higher allowance rates for PPH applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH applications tend to have higher allowance rates, reflecting reliance on prior allowable claims from a partner office. This metric supports choosing PPH when allowance probability improvement is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Average fewer rounds of prosecution for PPH cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH often reduces the number of office actions compared to standard prosecution, shortening overall prosecution lifecycle and costs. This ties into efficiency and lower prosecution burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage and Pendency Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH applications represent ~2% of USPTO filings; average first action pendency: ~7.5 months for PPH; average pendency for standard applications: 18-24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics provide empirical context for expected timelines and relative frequency of PPH usage; factor them into portfolio-level decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: same earliest priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: Same earliest priority date in both applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corresponding application in the second office must share the same earliest priority date as the application in the first (office of earlier examination). Verify priority/priority claim chains before filing a PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: allowability in first office
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of first examination has determined at least one claim allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A favorable ruling (at least one allowable claim) from the first office is a precondition to request PPH; you must supply evidence of that allowability (e.g., office action or allowance notice) when filing the PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: claim correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in second office must 'sufficiently correspond' to allowable claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims need not be identical but should sufficiently correspond in scope/limitations to the allowable claims from the first office. A claim correspondence table is required to explain how claims map between offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: availability of office actions and search results
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions and search results from first office available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit copies of relevant office actions and search results from the Office of First Filing/Examination; ensure these documents are accessible and translated where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing steps and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Required filing items: 1) File PPH request with the second office; 2) Submit copies of office actions from first office; 3) Submit copies of allowed claims from first office; 4) Provide claim correspondence table; 5) Submit search information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the enumerated procedural steps precisely. The claim correspondence table and search information are critical evidentiary documents; missing or inadequate documentation can lead to denial of PPH status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic consideration — When to use PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended scenarios: when you have a quickly granted European Search Report (EESR); after a positive Australia or Israel search result; when PCT international preliminary examination found claims allowable; for technology with short commercial life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PPH when speed to grant or quick resolution is commercially important, especially for technologies with short market lifecycles or when a favorable foreign search/examination result is already in hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic consideration — When NOT to use PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid PPH when initial application has narrow claims you don't want; when you want to delay examination; when initial application was incompletely examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request PPH if adopting the allowable claims would be strategically undesirable (e.g., they narrow claim scope you want to keep), if you prefer to defer examination for business reasons, or if the first-office examination is incomplete or unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT international applications can use PCT-PPH based on a positive Written Opinion or International Preliminary Report on Patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a positive written opinion or IPER exists, PCT-PPH can accelerate national/regional prosecution and avoid waiting for later national-stage examination delays. Ensure the PCT-phase documents meet the receiving office's evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with other acceleration options
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison table elements: PPH (First action ~5 months, $0 fee, requires allowable claims in another office); Track One (~12 months total, $4,200, <30 claims); Accelerated Examination (~12 months, $140, requires pre-exam search + statement); First Action Interview (timeline varies, $0, must request within 60 days of FAOM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose acceleration route based on desired timeline, cost tolerance, and eligibility constraints (e.g., claim count limits, required prior search/statement). PPH is often lowest-cost if eligibility is met, but other tracks may better fit specific needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: participating offices only
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH eligibility depends on whether the counterpart office is part of the Global PPH network or IP5 PPH; check current participating offices before planning strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: claim divergence and dependency on foreign examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires correspondence of claims (cannot have claims dramatically different); initial office of examination must conclude examination favorably first; quality of underlying foreign examination affects PPH outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH's effectiveness is contingent on the substantive thoroughness and conclusions of the first-office examination; if the foreign examination is superficial or the claims diverge substantially, the second office may not accept PPH or may still issue substantial rejections.
